Let’s talk about something that’s both simple and surprisingly hard—self-love.
Chapter Nine: The Ongoing Practice of Self-Love.
Self-love isn’t some final destination you cross off your list. It’s more like a daily practice—a bunch of small choices you make, especially in those quiet moments when nobody else is around.
Have you ever caught yourself thinking, “If I just heal this one thing, I’ll finally feel confident?” I get it. It’s easy to picture healing as a single, life-changing event, and confidence as something that magically shows up fully formed. But real life? It’s messier, and honestly, a lot more beautiful.
There will be days when those old doubts creep back in. Maybe you look in the mirror and only see your flaws. Or the world just feels... indifferent. On days like these, self-love is almost rebellious. It’s choosing not to believe the worst about yourself.
Sometimes, it’s as simple as playing your favorite song on repeat, taking a walk outside, or cooking a meal with extra care. These little rituals—they might seem ordinary, but they become your anchors.
Self-love also means drawing boundaries. It’s okay to say no to things that drain you or make you feel small. And sometimes, it’s about reaching out, admitting you can’t do it all by yourself. There’s a quiet strength in that honesty—a reminder that real strength isn’t about never needing anyone, but about knowing when to ask for help.
This journey is ongoing. You’ll hit setbacks. There will be disappointments and days when it feels like you’re not making any progress at all. But don’t forget, there are breakthroughs too—those flashes of clarity, bursts of real joy, and the quiet pride that comes from living true to your values.
Over time, self-love becomes less about big, dramatic gestures, and more about showing up for yourself, day after day. It’s forgiving yourself, trying again, and holding onto the belief that you’re worthy of kindness—especially your own.
If there’s one thing to remember, it’s this: self-love isn’t about being perfect. It’s about being patient, gentle, and willing to start over, as many times as it takes.
